qualitative.gate_3m_moat_note: Multifamily residential real estate lacks durable barriers to entry. In Camden's core Sunbelt markets (Texas, Florida, Georgia, North Carolina, Arizona), abundant developable land and private developer capital drive recurring supply waves that trigger rent concessions and cap rate compression. Tenants face minimal switching costs at 12-month lease expirations. Empirically, Camden's 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 4.8% falls well below the 12% hurdle, and same-property rental revenue growth (+0.8% in 2025, +1.3% in 2024) consistently lags inflation.
qualitative.note: Fails Gate 3b (ROIC < 12% and lack of pricing power, REJECT). Camden Property Trust's 5-year median GAAP ROIC of ~4.8% (and 2.5-3.5% TTM) falls far short of the 12% hurdle rate, reflecting the structural capital intensity and 4-6% cap rates of multifamily real estate. In addition, CPT lacks pricing power >= inflation due to massive cyclical supply waves across its core Sunbelt markets and near-zero tenant switching costs. Same-property revenue growth (+1.3% in 2024, +0.8% in 2025) lagged inflation, while operating expenses grew faster (+1.8% in 2024, +1.7% in 2025).
qualitative.evidence: Camden Property Trust owns and operates ~172 properties with ~58,759 apartment units primarily across Sunbelt markets. Historical capital efficiency shows 5-year median GAAP ROIC of 4.8% (TTM ROIC 2.5-3.5%), structurally constrained by 4-6% cap rates and heavy invested capital. Core FFO was $6.85 in 2024 and $6.88 in 2025 (~0.4% growth). Same-property performance reveals minimal pricing power amidst record multifamily deliveries: 2024 same-property revenue +1.3% vs expenses +1.8% (NOI +1.1%); 2025 same-property revenue +0.8% vs expenses +1.7% (NOI +0.3%), both lagging CPI inflation (~2.5-3.0%). Balance sheet leverage is sound for a REIT (Net Debt-to-EBITDA 3.8x, ~80% fixed rate, unsecured revolving facility), but lack of economic moat and sub-hurdle capital returns disqualify it from compounding status under Munger criteria.
